Button.isLoadingProp: isLoading#183:0 — BOOLEAN on the set; each of the 120 variants holds a Spinner instance named 'spinner' at child index 0, visible bound to the prop, Size tracking the button size (XSmall=12, Small/Default=16, Large=20) and stroke bound to the same variable as that variant's label.
Button.setNote: TWO sets: 76:300 'Button' (120 = Variant 6 × Style 5 × Size 4, + Label TEXT + isLoading BOOLEAN) and 260:1600 'Button/Icon-only' (the same 120 with the label suppressed). Separate sets, not a 4th axis: in code `iconOnly` makes the label unrenderable ({!iconOnly && label}), so they are mutually exclusive — same reasoning as Badge vs Badge/Category. Icon-only variants were CLONED from their labelled counterparts, so all fills/strokes/focus effects/theme bindings and the aiden flag/is-dark overlay carry over verbatim; only the label removal, squared padding (--p-1 xsmall, --p-2 else; icon 12/14/20/24px) and aiden's --rounded-full differ. The icon-only set carries an INSTANCE_SWAP property `Icon` pointing at the _Icon/* components on _Template (Plus, Copy, Check, Pencil, Trash, More, Send, Download). That slot is REQUIRED, not decoration: Figma forbids overriding vector geometry inside an instance, so a drawn glyph would have locked every instance to the placeholder. Examples frame now shows icon-only in three contexts (card header actions, toolbar, aiden send) in light and dark.
resolved: The Figma Button set modelled no iconOnly / icon slot, so components composing an icon-only Button (CodeBlock copy, ChatComposerSend) had nothing faithful to instance. Closed 2026-07-25 with the Button/Icon-only set. Also bound the Button set wrapper's padding/radius (previously raw 32px / 5px default) and fixed a 17px overflow — the page is now all-zeros on lint.

Button/Icon-only initially shipped with a drawn placeholder glyph, which made it nearly useless — instances could not change the icon. Reworked 2026-07-25: each variant's icon is now an instance of an _Icon/* component bound to an INSTANCE_SWAP property.

The 8 hand-drawn _Icon/* placeholders were replaced 2026-07-25 by the real lucide library: all 120 variants' icon instances swapped, the INSTANCE_SWAP default repointed to Icon/plus, 18 example instances remapped to their canonical equivalents (Trash->trash-2, More->ellipsis, Send->arrow-up), and the temporaries deleted.

Icon-only buttons rendered a flat 2px stroke at every size, which reads as a blob at 12-14px. Fixed 2026-07-25: each variant's icon vectors now carry 2 x size / 24 (XSmall 1.0, Small 1.167, Default 1.667, Large 2.0), matching the browser. Stroke colour bindings were also restored — swapComponent had discarded them.

Leading and trailing icon slots added 2026-07-25 to all 120 labelled variants — a boolean plus an instance-swap each. A LABELLED button's icon sizes are --w-3/-3-5/-4/-5 (12/14/16/20), which differ from icon-only's 12/14/20/24; each variant sets the matching Icon-collection mode so stroke weight stays right and survives a glyph swap.
Button.props: Button (76:300): VARIANT Variant x Style x Size + TEXT Label + BOOLEAN isLoading + BOOLEAN 'Leading icon' / INSTANCE_SWAP 'Leading glyph' + BOOLEAN 'Trailing icon' / INSTANCE_SWAP 'Trailing glyph' (mirror IconLeft / IconRight in code; both off by default). Button/Icon-only (260:1600): same variants + INSTANCE_SWAP Icon.

Spinner.themed: indirectly — no colour prop; renders currentColor, so a themed parent colours it
Spinner.notes: Non-interactive: no hover/focus/disabled, so the Spec frame is sizes × colour contexts plus a rotation-phase strip (Figma can't animate). Icon built via figma.createNodeFromSvg with lucide's LoaderCircle path, then rescale(size/24) so stroke stays 2÷24 of the box. Colour is set per-instance on the child VECTOR named 'loader-arc'.

Label.themingFrame: OMITTED — Label is neutral chrome (foreground / muted-foreground / error only). The omission is stated in the TOKENS section so it reads as a decision, not a gap.
Label.props: VARIANT Size (sm/default/lg) × VARIANT Disabled (False/True) = 6 variants; BOOLEAN Required + 'Show description'; TEXT Label + Description.
Label.notes: Disabled had to be a VARIANT, not a BOOLEAN: Figma booleans can only drive layer visibility, and disabled is opacity 50%. Overview carries an ANATOMY section because six components reuse the .ui-label__* class names rather than nesting <Label> — that split (5 render it / 6 borrow the classes) is the page's most important content.

Input.themingFrame: OMITTED — --ring / --focus / --border-hover / --bg-input-30 are Mode-level neutrals that no data-theme remaps. Stated in the TOKENS section.
Input.props: VARIANT Size (sm/default/lg) × Error (False/True) × Disabled (False/True) = 12; BOOLEAN 'Show label' / 'Show error message' / 'Icon left' / 'Icon right'; TEXT Placeholder / 'Error message'.
Input.notes: Nests a live Label instance with isExposedInstance=true, so Label's Required / Show description surface on any Input. Owns .ui-input-wrap — documented in the Overview as a CONTRACT because Textarea, NativeSelect, InputGroup and the Chat composer apply the class to their own markup rather than importing Input. When building those four, reuse this wrap spec verbatim; do not redefine borders. [Test-drive fix 2026-07-27] Added swappable Leading glyph (Leading glyph#668:0) + Trailing glyph (Trailing glyph#668:13) INSTANCE_SWAP properties across all 12 variants (default = Icon/search 312:20402), mirroring the code IconLeft/IconRight props — previously the icon was a hard-baked search vector with only a show/hide boolean. Verified: default shows search, swaps to any Icon/* (tested mail 312:19670).

Textarea.themingFrame: OMITTED — same neutral surface as Input; stated in TOKENS.
Textarea.props: VARIANT Size × Error × Disabled = 12; BOOLEAN 'Show label' / 'Show error message'; TEXT Placeholder / 'Error message'. No icon slots (a textarea has no room).
Textarea.notes: Reuses Input's wrap via --multi: wrap height auto + padding 0 + align stretch, padding moved onto the .ui-textarea so the native resize grip lands in the true corner. Min-heights 64/96/128 bound to height/16|24|32. The grip is drawn as an absolutely-positioned 2-tick vector named 'resize grip (native)' pinned to MAX/MAX constraints. TextareaSize re-exports InputSize so the two can't drift.

NativeSelect.themingFrame: OMITTED — same neutral surface as Input; stated in TOKENS.
NativeSelect.props: VARIANT Size × Error × Disabled = 12; BOOLEAN 'Show label' / 'Show error message'; TEXT Value / 'Error message'. No icon booleans — the right slot is permanently the chevron.
NativeSelect.notesInputGroupSibling: see InputGroup below — fourth and last wrap consumer
NativeSelect.notes: Third wrap consumer and the only one that uses .ui-input-wrap completely unmodified. Two things the page exists to teach: (1) the ours/browser boundary — the closed control is ours, the open list is browser/OS-rendered and unstylable (option color/background honoured on Windows+Linux, ignored on macOS), which is precisely why the floating Select exists; (2) the hit-area trick — the <select> gets margin-right -(--w-4 + --p-2) and equal padding-right so it bleeds under the pointer-events:none chevron, making the whole trailing edge open the menu, size-independently. NO open-state frame is drawn, deliberately: mocking one OS's menu would document a lie. NativeSelectOption/OptGroup get no Figma components (no visual form of ours).

InputGroup.setNote: 208:97 is InputGroup/Button — the ONLY sub-part modelled as a component set. 16 variants (4 variants × 4 sizes).
InputGroup.themingFrame: PRESENT — the first field component with one. InputGroupButton variant=default fills with --primary (Theme collection) and takes the Aiden gradient under data-surface. Everything else in the family is neutral.
InputGroup.props: InputGroup/Button: VARIANT Variant (default/outline/ghost/destructive) × Size (xs/sm/icon-xs/icon-sm) = 16; TEXT Label.
InputGroup.notes: COMPOUND-FAMILY PATTERN worth copying: of the 6 exports only InputGroupButton has real visual decisions, so only it becomes a component set. Addon / Text / Input / Textarea are layout containers whose look comes from the wrap plus their own padding — documented as SLOTS (a labelled order-0..4 diagram) plus a composition gallery of assembled examples, not modelled as components. Two techniques documented: (1) CSS order decouples visual placement from DOM order so the input always gets Tab first; (2) the doubled selector `.ui-input-field .ui-input-group__wrap` is required to out-specify Input's per-size padding rule — without it the leading edge double-pads (owner hit this bug in code earlier). In Figma the block addons are built as VERTICAL rows rather than emulating flex-wrap + flex-basis:100%; visually identical, far simpler.
InputGroup.slots: InputGroup/Button's `glyph` is a SLOT on the 8 icon-* variants (the icon was fixed geometry, changeable only by detaching). The 8 labelled variants keep the Label TEXT property — a short label is better served by text than by a slot. Matches the code: InputGroupButton takes children: React.ReactNode.

InputOTP.themingFrame: OMITTED — slot surface is neutral; stated in TOKENS.
InputOTP.props: VARIANT Size (sm/default/lg) × State (Empty/Focused/Partial/Complete/Error/Disabled) = 18; BOOLEAN 'Show label' / Separator / 'Show error message'; TEXT Label / 'Error message'.
InputOTP.notes: The ONE form control that does NOT reuse .ui-input-wrap — slots own their border, radius and focus ring, so forcing them through the wrap would mean fighting its padding/height per size. State is a WHOLE-CONTROL axis, not a per-slot one, because a slot is never designed alone; the Spec adds an isolated slot-state strip (default/active/filled/error/error-active) for the atomic view. Built at length 6 with a toggleable groupSize-3 separator. Caret = 2px bar, --w-0-5 wide, steps(1) blink on --duration-shimmer, shown only in the active EMPTY slot.

Checkbox.themingFrame: PRESENT — checked AND indeterminate fill with --primary (Theme collection); mark is --primary-foreground. Unchecked stays neutral.
Checkbox.props: VARIANT Size (sm/default/lg) × State (Unchecked/Checked/Indeterminate) × Disabled (False/True) = 18; BOOLEAN 'Show label' / 'Show description'; TEXT Label / Description.
Checkbox.notes: First Phase 2 page. Hidden-input pattern: the native <input> is opacity-0/0x0 (NOT display:none) so it stays focusable + submittable, and every visual state is a CSS sibling selector. Both SVGs (check + dash) are always mounted and overlaid so checked→indeterminate CROSS-FADES; stroke-dasharray 24 → dashoffset 0 draws the stroke in. Box carries margin-top --p-0-5 to sit against the first text line — in Figma that is a 'box align' wrapper frame since auto-layout has no per-child margin. Aiden is a SURFACE effect here (not a variant like Button), so it is documented in text only. Uses .ui-label__* classes rather than nesting <Label> (a label can't contain a label).

RadioGroup.setNote: 223:129 is RadioGroup/Item — the group root is a layout container + context provider, documented as composition per the compound-family rule.
RadioGroup.themingFrame: PRESENT — checked circle fills with --primary (Theme collection), dot is --primary-foreground.
RadioGroup.props: RadioGroup/Item: VARIANT Size (sm/default/lg) × State (Unchecked/Checked) × Disabled = 12; BOOLEAN 'Show label' / 'Show description'; TEXT Label / Description.
RadioGroup.notes: Same hidden-input pattern as Checkbox. DOCUMENTED DIVERGENCE: in code `size` is set ONCE on the group and cascades to every item via CSS descendant selectors; Figma cannot model a descendant selector reaching into instances, so each item carries its own Size and the Overview says so explicitly under a '⚠ CODE vs FIGMA' section. The group owns three things the items never receive as props: name/value/callbacks via React context, the size cascade via CSS, and role=radiogroup + aria-labelledby via ARIA. RadioGroupItem throws outside a RadioGroup because a nameless radio silently stops excluding its siblings. Label visibility bound to the ui-label CONTAINER (Checkbox lesson).

Switch.themingFrame: PRESENT — on-track fills with --primary (Theme collection). Off stays --muted in every theme, deliberately.
Switch.props: VARIANT Size (sm/default/lg) × State (Off/On) × Disabled = 12; BOOLEAN 'Show label' / 'Show description'; TEXT Label / Description.
Switch.notes: Third and last of the hidden-input trio. role='switch' on a native type=checkbox — keeps every native behaviour, only changes the announcement to 'switch, on/off'. Thumb travel (12/16/20px) is an intentional hard-coded literal per CLAUDE.md: travel = track − thumb − 2×2px inset. In Figma the thumb is an absolutely-positioned ellipse at x=2 (off) / x=2+travel (on). Overview carries a Switch-vs-Checkbox-vs-Radio decision guide (the distinction is immediacy, not appearance).
resolved: The 'default sits 2px low' alignment inconsistency was a SYMPTOM, not the cause: Switch never passed a size class to its label, so .ui-label__text stayed at --leading-5 (20px) at every size while the track scaled 16/20/24. The margin was patching that mismatch on the one size that least needed it. Fixed 2026-07-25 by adding ui-label--sz-{size} (matching Checkbox and RadioGroup) and deleting the --sz-default margin-top. Track height now equals label line-height at all three sizes (16/16, 20/20, 24/24), so every track is flush with no nudge. The ramps are now coupled — a comment in Switch.scss records that.

Slider.themingFrame: PRESENT — filled range AND the 3px thumb border read --primary. Unfilled track stays --muted.
Slider.props: VARIANT Size (sm/default/lg) × Mode (Single/Range) × Disabled = 12; BOOLEAN 'Show label' / 'Show value'; TEXT Label. Value text is intentionally NOT a bound property so Range variants can keep '25 – 75' while Single keeps '60' — text in an instance is directly editable anyway.
Slider.notes: The ONE form control with no hidden native input: <input type=range> has a single thumb, so range mode would need a second implementation. Each thumb is its own role='slider' span; ARIA here IS the implementation. Neighbour clamp lives in each thumb's aria-valuemin/max (announced, not just enforced). Position/width are deliberately NEVER transitioned — easing would lag the pointer during a drag; only box-shadow and border-color ease. Track uses overflow:visible so the focus ring escapes a 4px sm track. In Figma the thumb is an absolutely-positioned ellipse; Single sits at 60%, Range at 25%/75%.
Slider.layoutNote: Spec card is 1440 wide (not the usual 1280): 4 state columns × 290px cells overflowed a 1280 card by 22px. Measure row content against the TABLE's inner padding, not just the card bounds — the card-level lint misses this.

Badge.setNote: TWO sets: 236:70 'Badge' (12 status variants) and 236:161 'Badge/Category' (15 hues × soft|solid = 30). Split because `category` OVERRIDES `variant` in code — they are two modes, not two axes.
Badge.themingFrame: PRESENT — only default + outline follow the brand (--primary / --primary-text / --primary-border). The semantic four keep their own colour in every theme; the 15 category hues are a fixed palette and never theme.
Badge.props: Badge: VARIANT Variant (12) + TEXT Label. Badge/Category: VARIANT Hue (15) × Style (soft|solid) + TEXT Label.
Badge.notes: Category variables are NESTED in Figma: category/{hue}/base | /bg | /text (NOT hyphen-suffixed), plus a single category/foreground. The aiden variant is a real gradient variant (unlike Checkbox/Switch where aiden is only a surface effect), so it carries the aidenDarkPattern overlay bound to flag/is-dark — verified flipping. No size prop and no brand variant, both deliberate; stated on the page. Not interactive: a <div> with no role/tabindex, so the Spec has no hover/focus/disabled axis.
Badge.contrastNote: Soft category style is AA-gated (all 15 -text-on--bg pairings in npm run test:contrast). Solid is deliberately NOT gated — inverted --category-foreground dips under AA on amber/green in light. Owner's accepted call; the page says so plainly rather than hiding it.

Kbd.themingFrame: ABSENT — neutral chrome (--secondary surface). A keycap that changed colour per brand would read as a button.
Kbd.notes: The keycap look is an ASYMMETRIC border: strokeTopWeight/Left/Right bound to border-width/100 and strokeBottomWeight to border-width/300 — that thicker bottom edge is the whole illusion. minWidth is bound per size (width/4|5|6) so single characters (K, ⌘, ⇧) stay square while multi-character caps (Esc, Enter) widen past it. Font sizes come straight from the SCSS: sm and default are BOTH --text-xs (12px), only lg steps up to --text-sm (14px) — sm differs from default in box size, not type.

Separator.themingFrame: ABSENT — a rule that changed colour per brand would fight the content it divides.
Separator.notes: The labeled variant is a horizontal auto-layout of line/label/line with both lines set layoutSizingHorizontal='FILL' — that mirrors the CSS flex:1 on ::before/::after, so the word stays centred at any width. In code, setting a label forces orientation to horizontal. The vertical variant relies on align-self: stretch, so it needs a parent that gives it height; dropped into a block container it collapses to nothing (noted on the Spec frame). decorative → role='none' is the documented a11y decision.

StatusDot.themingFrame: ABSENT — semantic, not brand. A green 'online' must stay green in every sub-brand.
StatusDot.notes: The idea worth copying: each status sets ONE custom property (--ui-status-color) and both the dot and the ::after pulse ring read it back, so the colour is written once rather than twice per status. Modeled in Figma as a hidden 'pulse ring' ellipse at 0.35 opacity whose visibility is bound to a Pulse boolean. offline and neutral both resolve to --muted-foreground and therefore render identically — that is faithful to the code and deliberately called out on the page rather than hidden.

Skeleton.themingFrame: ABSENT — the --bg-primary-10 shimmer highlight IS technically themed, but a 10%-alpha sweep is imperceptible as a brand demo.
Skeleton.props: VARIANT Shape (default|circle|text). Width/height are free-form in code — resize the instance in Figma.
Skeleton.notes: The shimmer is a background-position animation on a 200%-wide gradient, not a moving element — nothing in the layout moves, which is why a page of skeletons stays smooth. Figma variables hold solid colours only, so the sweep is drawn as a white low-alpha GRADIENT_LINEAR overlay rather than bound. Make that overlay FULL-BLEED (same size as the shape, x=0, STRETCH constraints): a narrower band's own rect edge shows through the circle's round clip as a hard vertical line.

Code.setNote: TWO components: 252:35 'Code' is a single COMPONENT (inline chip, no variant axis — only a Label text prop); 252:59 'CodeBlock' is a 3-variant SET on a Header axis (filename | copy | none).
Code.themingFrame: ABSENT — neutral in every brand. Code should not change colour with the sub-brand.
Code.props: Code: TEXT Label. CodeBlock: VARIANT Header (3) + TEXT Filename + TEXT Code.
Code.notes: The Header axis mirrors real CSS behaviour: with no filename the header switches to justify-content: flex-end (hence the 'copy' variant pushes the button right), and with showCopy=false and no filename there is no header element at all. Documents the deliberate no-syntax-highlighting decision AND that 11 --code-* syntax tokens already exist in tokens.scss (mirrored to Figma as code/*) with zero consumers (now at least AA-gated) — a palette pre-picked for a highlighter we do not have. The Overview carries a syntax-palette REFERENCE (node 265:53) — 11 swatches rendered in mono on the real code/block surface, light and dark side by side, each labelled with its measured contrast. Deliberately a swatch table, NOT a highlighted CodeBlock instance: rendering one would document a capability the library does not have (same rule as NativeSelect's undrawn open state). It also makes both remaining judgment calls visible — attr-vs-number now separate in both modes, selector sharing string's hue obviously enough to read as intended. OWNER DECISION 2026-07-25: the Overview also carries two HIGHLIGHTED MOCK-UPS (node 267:57) — a .tsx and a .scss block, light and dark, between them exercising all 11 code/* tokens with every span bound to its variable. These are NOT CodeBlock instances and the component cannot render them; the owner accepted that designers may build with them and chose to defer the code decision (add a tokenizer dependency vs keep flat rendering) until something actually needs it. The labelled separator and the note directly beneath say so explicitly. Layer names mirror the real component so the intent transfers if it is ever built. This is a deliberate, owner-approved exception to the 'don't draw what isn't ours' rule — do not silently delete it, and do not treat it as licence to mock other unbuilt behaviour.
Code.figmaDivergence: Inline chip vertical padding is 0.1em in CSS (em-relative, ~1.3px at --text-code); Figma variables cannot express em, so it is bound to spacing/0-5 (2px). Stated on the Avatar Overview note covering both divergences.
resolved: The scrollable <pre> had overflow-x: auto with no tabindex, making overflowed code unreachable by keyboard (WCAG 2.1.1 / axe scrollable-region-focusable). Fixed 2026-07-25: tabIndex={0} plus an inset --focus ring in Code.scss. No ARIA role added, so it stays announced as preformatted text.

The 11 --code-* syntax tokens were an exact Tailwind 500/600 mapping that had never been contrast-checked; the script confirmed 10 of 11 below AA in light (2.22-4.29). Fixed 2026-07-25: light values darkened to Tailwind 600/700 (comment uses a derived slate #5e6d7d — the lightest that clears AA, so it stays recessive against --code-variable), and dark --code-attr moved orange-400 → amber-300 to break a collision with --code-number that existed in dark only. All 11 now gated in scripts/contrast-check.mjs (49 pairings, 0 below AA). Figma code/* variables synced. STILL A JUDGMENT CALL, deliberately left alone: --code-selector shares --code-string's hue in both modes (consistent, so it reads as intentional), and in dark --code-type (cyan-400) sits close to --code-function (sky-400).

The Overview composition note claimed the Figma Button set did not model iconOnly. Stale once Button/Icon-only shipped; corrected 2026-07-25. It now states that the copy control corresponds to Variant=Default/Style=Ghost/Size=XSmall/Icon=Copy and explains why it is still DRAWN rather than instanced inside the CodeBlock variants — the 2-second copied→check glyph swap would otherwise need a CodeBlock variant axis for a transient state no consumer controls.

CloseButton.themingFrame: ABSENT — a dismissal is never the themed action on a surface.
CloseButton.notes: The two variants are pixel-identical at rest and differ ONLY on hover (default shifts icon colour; background additionally fills --accent), which is why they are variants rather than separate components — the Spec matrix is built to make that the visible conclusion. Two a11y guarantees are designed in rather than documented around: the native aria-label is Omit-ed and replaced by an ariaLabel prop defaulting to 'Close' (so it can never ship nameless), and type='button' is hard-coded (so it can never submit a form). Focus is a box-shadow, not an outline, because the button is round and transparent.
resolved: Three defects fixed in code and mirrored 2026-07-25. (1) The hit target was 16x16, failing WCAG 2.5.8's 24x24 minimum on the library's most-tapped control; a transparent ::after now widens the pointer target without changing what is drawn. (2) stroke-width was pinned to --icon-border-width (1.33 VIEWBOX units), which halved to a 0.665px hairline at a 12px icon — the thinnest stroke in the library; removing the pin lets lucide's own width scale (1.0/1.33/1.67px), and at a 16px icon that lands on exactly 1.33px, so the token's VALUE was right and only the mechanism was wrong. (3) No size prop, leaving it the last interactive holdout of 26 components that have one — same reasoning that added size to Checkbox and RadioGroup in July. Toast keeps its density with size='sm' (that surface is why the small box existed); Dialog, Drawer, Alert and Banner move to default, whose X grows from a 12px icon in a 16px box to 16px in 24px.

Avatar.setNote: TWO sets: 254:69 'Avatar' (3 sizes × 2 shapes = 6, plus Image + Badge booleans and a Fallback text prop) and 254:184 'AvatarGroup' (3 Spacing variants, each holding 4 nested Avatar instances).
Avatar.themingFrame: ABSENT — a person's avatar is not a brand accent.
Avatar.props: Avatar: VARIANT Size × Shape + BOOLEAN Image + BOOLEAN Badge + TEXT Fallback. AvatarGroup: VARIANT Spacing (3).
Avatar.notes: The fallback is ALWAYS mounted at z-0 under the image rather than swapped in on error, so a slow image shows initials then resolves and a broken one shows initials permanently — no flash of empty space either way. The badge lives OUTSIDE __inner because __inner owns overflow:hidden to clip the image to the shape; a badge inside it would lose the half that overhangs. Modeled the image as a gradient placeholder rect (no asset uploads). Page updated to v1.1 after both defects were fixed in code — the Spec note now documents the resolution, not a reproduction.
Avatar.figmaDivergence: Initials carry --tracking-wide (0.025em) in code but plain tracking in Figma — pinning letterSpacing detaches textStyleId and 0.35px on two letters did not justify three new Semibold-Wide styles. Noted on the Overview frame.
resolved: AvatarGroup spacing ramp was non-monotonic (sm -8 / default -12 / lg -4). Fixed 2026-07-25 by reassigning the same three values in order: sm -12 / default -8 / lg -4. `spacing` names the visual gap, which runs inversely to the overlap. Groups that never set spacing loosen from -12 to -8, since default was the value out of place.

AvatarGroup `size` reached only the +N chip. Fixed 2026-07-25: the group now cloneElement's direct Avatar children that have no explicit size. Guarded on `child.type === Avatar` so a wrapping element (Tooltip, link) never receives `size` as an unknown prop; an explicit child size still wins.
Stories added: GroupSpacing + GroupSizeInheritance — the absence of these is why both survived.

AvatarGroup rendered flat-sided notches where avatars overlapped. Cause: the group's separating ring was applied to the instance ROOT, which had radius 0 — the circular shape lived only on ui-avatar__inner — so a 3px SQUARE ring was drawn around a circular avatar and its straight edge cut into the neighbour. Fixed 2026-07-25 by binding the root's radius per shape (circle -> radius/full, square -> radius/md), which also closes a fidelity gap: the CSS applies the radius to BOTH .ui-avatar and .ui-avatar__inner, and only the inner had been modelled.
Avatar.note: At Spacing=sm (-12px on a 40px avatar) the next circle clips part of the previous one's initials. That is faithful to the CSS, not a modelling error — worth knowing when choosing a spacing for two-letter fallbacks.

AspectRatio.themingFrame: ABSENT — and this one is absolute: AspectRatio.scss contains ZERO var(--…) references. It is the only component in the library that consumes no design token at all. Nothing to theme, and it never appears in the contrast script because it renders no text and no surface.
AspectRatio.notes: `ratio` is a CONTINUOUS number, not a union — any value is valid. Figma variants must be discrete, so the six are REPRESENTATIVE and the set description says so explicitly; this is a case where the Figma model cannot be faithful and the honest move is to label the shortcut. Also one of the few components with NO required `id` (rule 6 exception, like Toaster): no children of its own, no ARIA to wire, no state to announce. Documents the inline-style decision (ratio is per-instance, not a token; consumer `style` is spread after so it wins) and the one a11y trap — overflow: hidden clips the focus ring of any interactive child near the edge.
AspectRatio.manualStep: ⚠ Figma's aspect-ratio lock is READ-ONLY to plugins (node.targetAspectRatio cannot be assigned), so the six variants are sized correctly but not constrained — drag-resizing distorts them instead of deriving the height. Someone must select the six variants and enable the aspect-ratio lock (or set W and H to Scale) in the UI. Noted on the Spec frame and in the set description.

Blockquote.themingFrame: ABSENT — all neutral. Noted on the page that the 4px rule is a plausible place a brand accent COULD live (several design systems tint it) but this one keeps it --border, consistent with the rule that chrome stays neutral. Changing that would be a system decision, not a component tweak.
Blockquote.props: VARIANT Content (single|multi) + TEXT Quote + TEXT 'Quote 2' + BOOLEAN 'Show attribution' + TEXT Attribution.
Blockquote.notes: The Content axis exists to show the paragraph rule: `> p` has margin zeroed so a single-paragraph quote sits flush against the rule, and `> p + p` adds --p-3 back only between consecutive paragraphs — the default state needs no correction. `cite` is Omit-ed from the native props and REDEFINED as displayed content: HTML's own cite attribute takes a source URL that browsers never render, so the component trades machine-readable provenance for a better call site. No required `id` (leaf, no ARIA to wire). Added one text style, base/leading-7/Italic — the only 16/28 pairing in the system; the CSS is --text-base on --leading-7 and no existing style carried it.
Blockquote.specDeviation: ⚠ The HTML spec says a quotation's attribution must be placed OUTSIDE the blockquote (the canonical markup is <figure> + <figcaption>). This component renders a <footer> INSIDE, which is what most component libraries do and degrades gracefully, but strictly makes the attribution part of the quoted material. Documented on the a11y section rather than silently modelled as correct; fixing it would be a breaking DOM change.

ScrollArea.themingFrame: ABSENT — scrollbar chrome stays neutral; nothing reads --primary.
ScrollArea.props: VARIANT Orientation (vertical|horizontal|both). `type` (auto|hover) is NOT a variant — it changes nothing at rest that Figma can show, so it is a note.
ScrollArea.notes: The rails are LAID OUT, not overlaid: the inner element is a CSS grid where the viewport takes cell 1/1 and each rail gets its own fixed column/row with a --p-4 gap, so the thumb can never sit on content in any browser. The viewport needs min-width:0 / min-height:0 or the grid item refuses to shrink and the thing silently never scrolls. Thumb length and offset are computed at runtime from scrollTop/scrollHeight with a 20px floor, so the offsets drawn in Figma are ILLUSTRATIVE and the page says so. ResizeObserver watches the viewport and the children present AT MOUNT; a child that grows later is only caught by the layout effect keyed on `children`.
ScrollArea.codeFixesLandedSameDay: WCAG 2.1.1 — the viewport had no tabIndex, so 474px of content in a 206px box was unreachable by keyboard. Worse than the identical CodeBlock bug because the native scrollbar is hidden, leaving no fallback affordance, and because type='hover' keeps the rail at opacity 0 until :hover or :focus-within — which could never fire with nothing focusable inside. The two defects concealed each other; one tabIndex={0} fixed both. Also tokenized 5 raw opacity literals (ScrollArea x2, CloseButton, Chip, Command) and moved the thumb from cursor:pointer to grab/grabbing.

Chip.themingFrame: PRESENT — only the ACTIVE chip themes: it reads --primary for fill and border and --primary-foreground for the label. A resting chip is --bg-input-30 on --border, both neutral, so it is identical in every brand. The selection is the branded moment; the unselected state is chrome.
Chip.props: VARIANT Size (xsmall|small|default) × Active (false|true) = 6, + BOOLEAN 'Icon left'/'Icon right' with INSTANCE_SWAP glyphs + TEXT Label.
Chip.notes: Active is a VARIANT axis, not a boolean — it changes fill, border and text colour, and a Figma boolean can only drive visibility. Hover moves only the resting chip (--bg-input-30 → -50); the active rule re-states --primary so a selected filter does not shift under the cursor, and the base hover is scoped :not(.ui-chip--active). Verified the SCSS `:not(&--active)` compiles correctly to `:not(.ui-chip--active)`. Hit targets measured 26 / 34 / 38px tall — all clear the 24px minimum, xsmall being the tightest.
openQuestions: IconCenter is in ChipProps but does nothing distinct: the JSX renders {IconLeft}{IconCenter}{label}{IconRight}, so it occupies the same slot as IconLeft. With a label present the two are identical; without one it produces the same icon-only chip IconLeft would. Chip has no `iconOnly` switch (unlike Button) to suppress the label, and the container is justify-content: flex-start so nothing ever centres. Either wire it to suppress+centre like Button, or remove it — removing is breaking. Documented on the Overview as an alias for now.

An icon-only Chip has NO accessible name. `aria-label` is an optional prop with no fallback, so <Chip IconLeft={X} /> announces only 'button, not pressed'. CloseButton solves the identical problem by defaulting ariaLabel to 'Close'. Consider the same default, or requiring aria-label when no label is passed (a discriminated union would enforce it).

Toggle.themingFrame: ABSENT and DELIBERATE — pressed fills neutral --accent, never --primary. A toolbar is a row of toggles and a screen has one primary action; if Bold/Italic/Underline all lit up in the brand colour they would out-shout the CTA beside them. Same reasoning as the ghost-button carve-out. Chip is the component that DOES take the brand when pressed.
Toggle.props: VARIANT Variant (default|outline) × Size (sm|default|lg) × Pressed (false|true) = 12, + BOOLEAN Icon + INSTANCE_SWAP Glyph + TEXT Label.
Toggle.notes: Chip-vs-Toggle is the decision this page exists to settle: does the on-state change WHAT DATA is shown (Chip, brand fill) or HOW A TOOL BEHAVES (Toggle, neutral fill)? ToggleGroup does not re-implement any of this — its items reuse .ui-toggle and collapse shared borders ButtonGroup-style, so changing Toggle changes the segmented control. Controlled/uncontrolled boundary is `pressed !== undefined`, so pressed={false} is controlled but omitting it is not — a computed prop that flips to undefined silently hands control back.
Toggle.openQuestion: ⚠ Hover and pressed resolve to the SAME fill (--accent), so an unpressed toggle under the cursor looks identical to a pressed one at rest. In a toolbar this reads fine because the pointer is over only one item and the rest show true state; a LONE borderless toggle is genuinely ambiguous. Documented on the Spec frame with the outline variant recommended as the mitigation. Not changed — distinguishing them would mean a new hover token or a pressed treatment beyond fill, which is a system decision.

ToggleGroup.themingFrame: ABSENT — inherits Toggle's neutral pressed state, deliberately.
ToggleGroup.notes: Items are NOT Toggle instances in code either — ToggleGroupItem is a <button> wearing .ui-toggle, because it reads pressed state from context rather than owning it. ToggleGroup.scss therefore has NO colour/size/state rules; it only arranges. The segmented recipe is three rules: flatten inner radii, collapse borders with margin -1px (--border-w-100), and lift the active item to z-index 1 so its ring/fill is not clipped by an overlapping neighbour. In Figma the items are DRAWN, not Toggle instances, because per-item corner flattening cannot be expressed by an instance whose radius is bound uniformly — stated in the set description.
openQuestions: No arrow-key navigation. The WAI-ARIA toolbar pattern expects a roving tabindex (one tab stop, arrows move within); here every item is its own tab stop. Workable at 3-5 items, which is why the page caps the recommended length. Menubar in this library DOES implement roving tabindex, so the pattern exists if this is worth closing.

The group has no accessible name. role="group" with no aria-label announces just 'group'. Unlike the item-level name (now type-enforced), nothing requires this. Could default one, or require aria-label on the root.
type="single" deselect passes an EMPTY STRING, not undefined — onValueChange is typed (value: string) => void and the code sends `next ?? ''`. Consumers must treat '' as 'nothing selected'.

ButtonGroup.themingFrame: ABSENT — every token ButtonGroup itself reads is neutral (--border, --secondary). Stated in TOKENS. The colour in the examples belongs to the child Buttons, which do theme.
ButtonGroup.props: VARIANT Orientation (horizontal|vertical) = 2. Deliberately no Style/Size axis — those belong to the child Buttons, not the group.
ButtonGroup.notes: Three components, mirroring the three exports: ButtonGroup (2 variants), ButtonGroup/Separator (Orientation, 2) and ButtonGroup/Text (1). The root models ONLY orientation because that is its only prop — adding a style axis would have repeated Badge's variant/category mistake of offering choices the API does not have. Spec is 'anatomy x orientation' rather than 'matrix x states': the group is a div with role=group and has no states of its own, so the table breaks down seam treatment by position (first/middle/last), orientation, the two drawn parts, and the focus lift. Shipped WITH a code fix — see the ButtonGroup entry in git history.
openQuestions: role="group" has no accessible name and nothing enforces one; consumers must pass aria-label. Same gap as ToggleGroup.
ButtonGroupText is a <div>, not a <label>, so a visible 'Sort by' cell is not programmatically tied to the buttons.

On the solid default style the focus ring is --primary-focus — the fill colour at 40% alpha — so where it crosses a neighbouring solid button it is invisible even with the z-index lift. Fixing it means changing Button's focus token globally, not ButtonGroup. Ring reads fully only on transparent-fill styles.
ButtonGroupSeparator exposes role="separator" to AT; aria-hidden may be more honest where it is decorative.

Card.themingFrame: ABSENT — Card is neutral chrome; nothing in it reads --primary. Stated in TOKENS.
Card.props: NO variant axis. One assembled `Card` COMPONENT with TEXT props (Title, Description, Body) and BOOLEAN props (Show description, Show header action, Show footer), plus Card/Header, Card/Body and Card/Footer as standalone region specimens. `interactive` is modelled as code-only: it has NO resting appearance, only cursor + hover/focus, which are drawn in Spec.
Card.newTextStyle: base/leading-5/Semibold (16/20) — created for the card title; base/leading-normal is 24 and base/leading-none is 16.
Card.notes: First Phase 3 page. Deliberately NOT a variant set: the only prop that could be an axis (`interactive`) looks identical at rest, and this file's convention (set by Button) is that states live in the Spec table, not as variants. Region components exist because a Figma instance cannot take children, so a designer building a custom card needs the three parts separately. Spec is 'anatomy x states'. Ships with a code fix — the interactive card now carries the system focus ring. | 2026-08-08: gained CardMedia. Also note a SLOT conversion does not report its new type within the SAME use_figma call — the node still reads FRAME and only reads SLOT on the next call. Verify conversions in a fresh call or you will conclude, wrongly, that it failed.
openQuestions: CardHeader generates `${id}-title` on its heading but nothing in the library references it — it exists for a consumer to point aria-labelledby at.
CardBody and CardFooter take no `id` prop, unlike Card and CardHeader — inconsistent with hard rule 6, probably deliberate since they are layout-only.
overflow:hidden clips any menu/popover/tooltip opened inside a card; those need a portal.
CardHeader always renders an <h3>; the level is not configurable, so a card can produce a heading order that does not match its document position. Still open after the media addition.
Card.slots: FIVE slots: ui-card__media (NEW), ui-card__header-media, ui-card__header-action, ui-card__body, ui-card__footer — on the assembled Card and on each region component. All are React.ReactNode in code. Title/Description/Body stay TEXT props.
Card.codeChange: CardHeader gained `media?: React.ReactNode` (2026-07-26). Card was the only one of the four media families without a leading slot — ItemMedia, EmptyMedia and AttachmentMedia already existed. Driven by the Figma side: a whole-header slot would have let a designer draw a featured icon no developer could build.
Card.cardMedia:
ADDED 2026-08-08, code first then mirrored — the playbook's own rule, and the same route that produced CardHeader.media.

THE TWO MEDIA ROLES ARE NOT THE SAME THING, and conflating them is what made this confusing. ui-card__header-media is a LEADING visual on the title's own line — avatar, status dot, featured icon. It can never be a cover: in CSS it is flex-shrink:0 inside the header's flex row, icon-sized, floored at one line of title. ui-card__media is the full-bleed COVER.

It is a sibling PART, not a `media` prop on Card, because a prop must choose an order; as a part the caller can place the cover above the header, between header and body, or last.

Code composes AspectRatio at a default 16 / 9 so a grid keeps a level top edge and nothing shifts as images load. It declares NO radius — .ui-card is overflow:hidden, so a cover touching an edge inherits the rounding; adding one shows as a hairline of card background in the corners.

Figma: "Show cover" BOOLEAN defaults to FALSE, so no existing Card instance grew a cover when the property landed. Card/Media (1233:25901) is the standalone region component.

Item.themingFrame: ABSENT — Item is neutral chrome; nothing reads --primary. Stated in TOKENS.
Item.props: Item: VARIANT Variant (default|outline|muted) x Size (xs|sm|default) = 9. Item/Media: Variant (default|icon|image) x Size = 9. Item/Separator: 1 component. TEXT Title + Description; BOOLEAN Show description/media/actions/header/footer; SLOT media/actions/header/footer, each with preferredValues + description. href / onClick / disabled are code-only — they change the ELEMENT, not the look.
Item.slots: FIRST page built slots-first. header and footer are PURE slots with NO text property — ItemHeader/ItemFooter take children: React.ReactNode in code, not a string. Title and description remain TEXT props because they are genuinely strings.
Item.notes: The row is a CSS GRID (grid-template-areas: header spans / media-content-actions / footer spans). Figma has no grid, so each variant nests an auto-layout row named 'row — media · content · actions'; identical render, stated on the page. Ships with a code fix — grouped rows now collapse touching borders and the focused row lifts to z-index 1, the third component to need that after ToggleGroup and ButtonGroup.
openQuestions: ItemGroup is role="list" and ItemSeparator role="separator", but the rows are NOT role="listitem" — the list is announced with no matching item count.
The actions slot sits inside the row, so if the row is a link or button anything interactive in actions is a nested interactive. Nothing prevents it.
Title is nowrap+ellipsis and description clamps to 2 lines, both with no title attribute — truncated text is unavailable to hover and to assistive tech alike.
disabled sets pointer-events: none, so a disabled row cannot show a tooltip explaining why.

Attachment.themingFrame: ABSENT — neutral chrome plus the error family; nothing reads --primary. Stated in TOKENS.
Attachment.props: Attachment: VARIANT Orientation (horizontal|vertical) x Size (xs|sm|default) = 6. Attachment/Media: Variant (icon|image) x Size (xs|sm|default|vertical) = 8. TEXT Title + Description; BOOLEAN Show description/media/actions; SLOT media + actions with preferredValues and descriptions.
Attachment.axisDecision: `state` is deliberately NOT a variant axis, following the Spinner precedent of adapting axes with a stated reason. It has 5 values but only 3 renderings — idle==done, uploading==processing (shimmer only), error is the single real repaint. Five near-identical variants would have been noise; the five are laid out as a row in Spec instead and the reasoning is on the Overview.
Attachment.notes: Parallel family to Item. The interesting technique is the two-layer overlay: __trigger is position:absolute inset:0 at z-index 1 so the whole card is clickable, __actions sit at z-index 2 so buttons are not swallowed, and isolation:isolate on the root keeps both out of the page stacking context. Neither layer is drawable (a transparent overlay renders as nothing) so Spec specifies rather than mocks it. Content is NOT a slot — see lessons.
openQuestions: `state` drives colour and a shimmer only; nothing is announced. A screen reader is told nothing when a file goes uploading -> done. Needs the state in the description text or a consumer-supplied aria-live region.
A card with a trigger plus three actions is four tab stops.
AttachmentTrigger's accessible name is entirely whatever children the consumer passes into the sr-only span; an empty trigger announces as a blank link the size of the card. Nothing enforces it.
Attachment.codeChanges: Three fixes shipped with this page: the error description no longer fades to 3.68:1 (last component applying o-80 to semantic text); AttachmentGroup is a keyboard-reachable scroll region; and the action button's hit target expands to 24x24 at xs. That last one exposed that CloseButton, AttachmentAction and the Chat composer tools had each hand-rolled the same shell, so `.ui-icon-button` was extracted to src/styles/icon-button.scss and all three now sit on it.

Collapsible.themingFrame: ABSENT — reads no colour beyond --foreground on the root. Stated in TOKENS.
Collapsible.props: VARIANT State (closed|open) = 2. EVERY prop is code-only: open/defaultOpen drive the one visual axis, onOpenChange and disabled have no resting appearance — a disabled Collapsible looks exactly like a closed one, because the disabled styling belongs to whatever Button was passed to the trigger.
Collapsible.notes: Spec IS the three-layer clip — that is the whole component. Also documents that CollapsibleTrigger renders no markup at all: it clones its single child and injects id / aria-expanded / aria-controls / data-state / disabled / onClick (the consumer's handler runs first, then the toggle). The header row in every example is labelled 'YOUR markup, not the component' because it genuinely is — Collapsible owns only the flex column and the clip. Ships with a code fix: the third clip layer was missing.
openQuestions: CollapsibleTrigger clones its child with `disabled`. Give it a non-button element and React warns about an unknown DOM attribute; nothing in the types prevents it.
`disabled` has no root-level styling — a disabled Collapsible is visually identical to a closed one. Consumers who care must style off data-disabled themselves.

Accordion.themingFrame: ABSENT — reads only neutral tokens. Stated in TOKENS.
Accordion.props: The SET is Accordion/Item with VARIANT State (closed|open|disabled) = 3 — that is the one visual axis. type (single|multiple), collapsible, value, defaultValue and disabled are all CODE-ONLY: single vs multiple look identical, the difference is purely whether opening one item closes the others.
Accordion.notes: NO code change — the component was already sound: three-layer clip, inert-when-closed, roving arrow-key focus (Up/Down + Home/End, disabled triggers skipped), single/multiple modes, all verified in the browser. Modelled as Accordion/Item (the repeating unit with the visual decisions) plus assembled 3-item lists drawn from mkItem, since the divider hairline is per-item (removed on the last). Shares Collapsible's grid-rows clip; the page cross-references it rather than re-explaining.
openQuestions: The trigger is a <button>, not a heading — the component makes no assumption about heading level, so a document that needs an outline must wrap the AccordionTrigger in its own <h3>.
A full-width trigger's 3px focus ring exits the container on both sides; fine standalone, but a consumer who wraps the Accordion in an overflow:hidden card will clip it left and right.

Alert.themingFrame: PRESENT — the brand variant is the ONLY one that themes. It reads --primary and follows data-theme; the four semantic variants (info/success/warning/error) keep their own colour under every theme. The theme grid shows the brand alert across all 9 codes.
Alert.props: VARIANT Variant (default|brand|info|success|warning|error) × Style (default filled | outline) = 12. TEXT Title + Description; BOOLEAN Show icon / Show description. Icon (any LucideIcon), action (ReactNode) and onClose are code-only. role is DERIVED not a prop: alert for error/warning, status otherwise.
Alert.supersedes: Parked pre-v4 Alert set 16:97 (6 variants, Type axis only, no style axis) DELETED from page 14:60. The Banner set 15:90 on that page is left until Banner ships.
Alert.notes: NO code change — verified sound: the July a11y sweep removed the opacity:0.8 that dropped semantic descriptions to 3.68 (now full colour, error 4.72 AA, gated by scripts/contrast-check.mjs). Filled description takes the semantic accent colour; outline description is muted-foreground. The 12-variant set was built HORIZONTAL+WRAP; the brand variant binds to the THEME collection (primary-light 2:47 / primary-border 2:49 / primary-text 35:65), everything else to Mode-level semantic vars.
openQuestions: The dismiss X inherits the variant colour at --o-70; on a filled error the muted X is coloured error too. Legible but worth a glance in a real red alert.
Icon is a LucideIcon prop with a per-variant default; the Figma set draws the default but does not model icon-swap (no INSTANCE_SWAP) — a designer changing the icon detaches.

Banner.themingFrame: PRESENT — brand variant only, same rule as Alert. The theme grid shows full-bleed brand bars across all 9 codes.
Banner.props: VARIANT Variant (default|brand|info|success|warning|error) = 6 (NO style axis, unlike Alert). TEXT Title, BOOLEAN Show icon. Icon, action, onClose and `centered` are code-only. `centered` is a LAYOUT mode (caps content at --max-w-5xl + centres), not a boolean-toggleable property, so it is shown in Examples not modelled as an axis. role derived: alert for error/warning, status otherwise.
Banner.supersedes: Parked pre-v4 Banner set 15:90 DELETED from page 14:60. Both parked sets (Alert + Banner) now retired; the migrate page 14:60 is empty.
Banner.notes: NO code change — the page-level cousin of Alert, verified sound. Full-bleed: a BOTTOM hairline (border-bottom-color) instead of Alert's all-round border, no radius, spans 100% width. Reuses Alert's semantic tint tokens verbatim (do not fork them). No muted description — the whole message takes the accent colour, AA-gated the same way. __close sits OUTSIDE __inner so it stays right-pinned when centred. Same THEME-collection binding for brand as Alert.
openQuestions: A Banner mounted at page load with role=alert (error/warning) announces immediately — intended for an outage bar, but a designer must not set a marketing message to error/warning or it interrupts on load.
`centered` cannot be a Figma property (it changes layout, not visibility); shown in Examples only, so an instance cannot be toggled to centred — a designer wanting it detaches or rebuilds.

Empty.themingFrame: ABSENT — neutral chrome; nothing reads --primary. The example Button themes on its own, the Empty container never does. Stated in TOKENS.
Empty.props: VARIANT Media (default | icon) = 2 — the one visual axis (EmptyMedia's variant). TEXT Title + Description; BOOLEAN Show description / Show action; SLOT media + content. Everything is children in code — Empty has no props of its own beyond EmptyMedia's variant. Static, no interactivity.
Empty.notes: NO code change — a clean static compound. Centred column, generous --p-12 vertical padding, header capped at --max-w-sm. icon media = a --w-12 --muted tile at --rounded-xl; default = an unboxed --w-10 glyph. The tile uses --muted (not --secondary) because it is an image surface carrying an icon, the same call Item/Attachment make. Modelled with Media as the variant axis; the icon and the action row are slots.
openQuestions: Empty is a plain <div> with no role — correct for a presentational block, but when it replaces a live region (a search-results list) the announcement must happen on that region, not here. Nothing enforces it.
The description is capped in Figma at a fixed 250px width; in code it is --max-w-sm (384) and wraps fluidly. The fixed width is a Figma approximation, not the code cap.
Empty.fixNote: 2026-07-27: the icon media tile rendered 48x32 (a wide blob) not 48x48. Cause: after converting ui-empty__media to a SLOT, a blanket layoutSizingVertical='HUG' pass (meant to clear stale slot heights) collapsed the height to hug the 24px glyph while the width stayed pinned at --w-12. Restored to a fixed 48x48 square, both axes bound. Empty was the ONLY slot affected — Item/Attachment media slots hold square Media INSTANCES, so hugging them stays square; Empty's slot held the tile styling directly.

Progress.themingFrame: PRESENT — the DEFAULT variant themes (indicator reads --primary), recoloured across all 9 codes; semantic variants keep their own hue.
Progress.aiden: YES — first Phase 3 component with an aiden gradient. The default determinate bar's indicator takes the violet→blue gradient under data-surface=aiden, built with the dark-overlay pattern (aiden-dark-gradient rect, visibility bound to flag/is-dark 175:26). Plus a completion particle burst (aiden-gated, not drawable). Documented in a dedicated AIDEN SURFACE card, since the flow + particles are animated.
Progress.props: VARIANT Variant (default|success|warning|error|info) × Size (sm|default|lg) = 15, laid out as a 5-row × 3-col grid (manual positioning after combineAsVariants). value/max/indeterminate/valueFormatter are code-only; label + showValue are header shortcuts.
Progress.notes: NO code change — the July a11y sweep already wired aria-labelledby to the rendered label via useId. Track --muted, indicator --primary (or variant colour), heights --h-1/-2/-3. The set cells are bare track+indicator (header shown once in anatomy) to keep the 15-grid tight. indeterminate is a 40% sliding bar with NO aria-valuenow — shown as its resting 40% frame, not drawable. value text uses tabular-nums.
openQuestions: Naming: `label` auto-wires aria-labelledby, but the compound API or a label-less bar needs a consumer aria-label — an unnamed progressbar announces only 'progress bar, 62%'.
The set cells omit the header row for grid density; a designer wanting the label+value composes it (shown in anatomy and examples) rather than toggling a property.

FeaturedIcon.themingFrame: PRESENT — brand variant only; reads --primary, recoloured across all 9 codes.
FeaturedIcon.props: VARIANT Variant (default|brand|success|warning|error|info) × Shape (square|circle) = 12 at default size. Size (sm|default|lg = 32/40/48) shown in Spec, not a variant axis (would be 36). Icon + label code-only.
FeaturedIcon.newComponent: YES — 58th component, added 2026-07-27. Extracted from the boxed icon-tile pattern hand-rolled in Empty, Item and Attachment media. Owner requested it after spotting the Empty tile. Index board got a new FeaturedIcon row (444:289).
FeaturedIcon.notes: Reuses Alert/Badge -light tint tokens, no new tokens. Icon is half the box at every size (16/20/24). Square radius scales md/lg/xl; circle is full. brand binds to Theme collection like Alert/Banner. Follow-up chip spawned to consolidate Item/Attachment/EmptyMedia tiles onto it.
FeaturedIcon.composedBy: WHERE FeaturedIcon should appear as a composed element / slot preferred value: Empty (icon media — code composes it; slot pref + uses-inside updated 2026-07-27), Card (ui-card__header-media slot — pref added 2026-07-27). TODO when built: Dialog + AlertDialog (a featured icon atop a confirmation — especially a red error tile for destructive confirms), ChatGreeting (centered featured icon on the start screen). Wire FeaturedIcon into those header/greeting areas + their slot preferredValues when their pages are built.

Tabs.themingFrame: ABSENT — the active pill is --background, not --primary; all neutral. Stated in TOKENS.
Tabs.props: VARIANT Orientation (horizontal|vertical) = 2. value/defaultValue/onValueChange/activationMode are code-only (selection + automatic-vs-manual activation aren't drawable). TabsContent unmounts unless forceMount.
Tabs.notes: NO code change — full WAI-ARIA tab pattern verified: roving tabindex (active=0, rest=-1), arrow + Home/End, automatic (arrow selects) vs manual (Enter/Space selects), focusable tabpanel. Active trigger is a lifted --background pill with --shadow-sm on a --muted list; inactive --muted-foreground. The trigger COLOUR is deliberately NOT transitioned (only bg+shadow) to dodge the Chromium var()-freeze on a live mode switch — documented on the page.

Breadcrumb.themingFrame: ABSENT — neutral chrome, no --primary. Links --muted-foreground, current page --foreground. Same stance as Tooltip / Sidebar; stated in TOKENS.
Breadcrumb.props: Atom components (mirrors the compound code, NOT one fixed trail): Breadcrumb/Crumb — VARIANT Type (link|current) + TEXT Label (link=--muted-foreground <a>, current=--foreground <span aria-current>); Breadcrumb/Separator — VARIANT Glyph (chevron|slash), aria-hidden; Breadcrumb/Ellipsis — single component. Every trail on the page (overview, spec cells, all six example trails) is COMPOSED FROM REAL INSTANCES of these, so they stay in sync with the masters and a designer drags atoms to build any depth.
Breadcrumb.notes: NO code change. Verified in-browser the link's `transition: color` does NOT hit the Chromium var()-transition freeze Tabs dodged: the link colour is `inherit` (the --muted-foreground var lives on the untransitioned .ui-breadcrumb parent), so a plain mode flip settles to the correct dark value (8.93:1) — documented on the a11y frame. REBUILT from a fixed hand-drawn trail to instanceable ATOMS after the owner asked why examples weren't the real component: Crumb/Separator/Ellipsis are real components, and overview + spec + examples compose instances (dark frames set Mode=Dark so the instances flip automatically — verified). Separator glyphs are lucide icon instances (chevron 312:18466, slash 312:20530, ellipsis 312:18936) stroke re-weighted (2·rendered/24) and bound to --muted-foreground. Hover cell overrides the link instance text fill to --foreground; focus cell wraps a link instance in a Focus/Default effect frame (2px pad bound to spacing/0-5). Lint all-zeros, no overflow, index row 125:396 linked.

Field.themingFrame: ABSENT — neutral scaffolding, drives no --primary. The only colour it owns is --error (invalid label + FieldError). Stated in TOKENS.
Field.props: Instanceable, composes real controls: Field — VARIANT Orientation (vertical|horizontal) + a Control SLOT (default = an Input instance, preferredValues Input/Checkbox/Switch) + TEXT Label/Description/Error + BOOL Required/Show description/Show error. Field/Legend — VARIANT (legend|label) + TEXT. invalid + disabled are DEMONSTRATED states (override the label fill to --error / set opacity 0.5), not variants. FieldSet/FieldGroup/FieldContent are spacing frames; FieldSeparator reuses the Separator component.
Field.notes: NO code change. Built instanceable per the Breadcrumb lesson: every field on the page (overview, spec cells, all example forms) is a real Field INSTANCE with a real control in the slot. The Control slot holds an Input instance by default with its built-in label turned OFF via 'Show label#192:0'=false (else Field's label doubles the Input's). The Checkbox example swaps the slot: hide slot.children[0] (the default Input), then slot.appendChild(Checkbox instance) — appending does NOT replace, so the default must be hidden. Dark frames set Mode=Dark and the nested control + text instances flip automatically (verified). GOTCHAS hit: resize() on an auto-layout frame freezes BOTH sizing axes to FIXED — the vertical variant's height froze at 10px until primaryAxisSizingMode was re-set to AUTO after the resize; and a hug-width group must be counterAxisSizingMode=AUTO with children NOT set to FILL, or the wrapped inputs squish. Lint all-zeros, no overflow, index row 125:406 linked.

Pagination.themingFrame: PRESENT (488:182) — the active cell borders/text read --primary-border / --primary-text, so it themes; shown under Main/db/dr/ph. Ghost cells + prev/next stay neutral.
Pagination.props: Instanceable atoms, cells reuse the Button visual: Pagination/Cell — VARIANT State (default|active) + TEXT Number (default=ghost --secondary-foreground; active=outline inset --primary-border + --primary-text + semibold, aria-current). iconLibrary.source: Generated from node_modules/lucide-react@1.24.0 in this repo — the SAME package the components import at runtime, so the Figma set cannot drift from what the code can render. Regenerate after a lucide upgrade; never hand-add icons.
iconLibrary.naming: Icon/{kebab} exactly as lucide names them (Figma 'circle-alert' = React CircleAlert).
iconLibrary.geometry: 24x24 masters at stroke-width 2 (lucide's native geometry). CRITICAL: lucide's stroke-width is in VIEWBOX units, so in the browser it scales with the icon — 12px renders 1.0px, 14px 1.167px, 16px 1.33px, 20px 1.667px, 24px 2.0px (measured in Storybook, not derived). Figma does NOT scale stroke on resize, so any instance placed below 24px must have its stroke set to 2 x size / 24 or it looks like a blob. Button/Icon-only carries the correct value per size. CloseButton is the carve-out: its CSS pins stroke-width to --icon-border-width (1.33 units) so at 12px it renders 0.665px.
iconLibrary.colour: Stroke bound to color/foreground; a host component (Button, Alert) overrides it, mirroring `color: inherit` in CSS. 25 icons have FILLED shapes (chart-scatter dots etc.) — those fills are bound too.
iconLibrary.aliases: 249 lucide aliases (alert-circle -> circle-alert, home -> house) deliberately EXCLUDED — duplicate geometry under an old name, and two identical entries in a swap list is worse than one findable one.
iconLibrary.licence: Lucide is ISC. The notice lives in node_modules/lucide-react/LICENSE; each component description records its lucide name and licence.
iconLibrary.pipeline: Do NOT paste icon data through the conversation — 353 KB of markup. Generate one SVG with each icon in <g id='{name}'> (the id becomes the Figma layer name), upload via the upload_assets tool + curl, then convert the imported groups to 24x24 components in chunks of ~450 (about 85ms each).
iconLibrary.layerNaming: Every icon's inner layers are uniform — a 'glyph' group over 'path-1', 'path-2', … — and this is load-bearing, not tidiness. Figma matches instance overrides BY LAYER NAME, so uniform names are what let a swapped icon keep the stroke colour and weight its host component set. Per-glyph names ('plus-1') silently reset both on every swap.
iconLibrary.strokeWeightMechanism: Collection 'Icon' (VariableCollectionId:291:32), modes 24/20/16/14/12, variable icon/stroke-weight. lucide's stroke-width is in VIEWBOX units, so the rendered value is 2 x size / 24. At 24/16/12 that lands exactly on the existing Primitives tokens, so those three modes ALIAS them: 24 -> icon-border-width/lg (2), 16 -> icon-border-width/default (1.33), 12 -> icon-border-width/sm (1). Modes 20 (1.667) and 14 (1.167) are intermediates of the same ratio with no token of their own — the code expresses this as a ratio, not a set of constants, so inventing tokens for them would be backwards. All ~6,971 icon vectors bind strokeWeight to the variable; each Button/Icon-only variant sets its size mode; the Icons page grid is pinned to mode 16 so the library displays at 1.33, the system's most common icon weight.
iconLibrary.warning: NEVER type a raw stroke weight on an icon in the Figma UI — it DETACHES the variable binding. That happened on 2026-07-25 (all 6,971 vectors detached to a flat 1.33) and had to be rebound. Change the MODE, not the value.
iconLibrary.swapGuidance: Change a glyph via the component's Icon / Leading glyph / Trailing glyph PROPERTY, not by selecting the nested icon layer and swapping it in the right panel. Both keep the 24x24 sizing, but a direct layer swap DROPS the strokeWeight variable binding (verified 2026-07-25), so the icon silently stops tracking the size mode.
iconLibrary.colourDurability: RESOLVED / was a mis-diagnosis. I previously recorded that an INSTANCE_SWAP discards the icon's stroke colour. Re-tested 2026-07-25 on Default/Default/Default, Error/Ghost/Small and Aiden/Default/Default, for both the icon-only set and the labelled Button's leading slot: swapping via the PROPERTY preserves the bound stroke colour AND the bound stroke weight in every case. The broken instances I originally measured had been damaged by my own swapComponent() rewire step, not by the property mechanism — I diagnosed the mechanism from wreckage I had created. The real, still-true caveat is narrower: swapping the nested icon LAYER directly (right panel, with the layer selected) drops the strokeWeight binding. Use the property.
iconLibrary.colourModel: OWNER DECISION 2026-07-25: icons do NOT auto-tint. They arrive as --foreground and the designer sets the colour after placing. Automatic per-variant tinting was attempted five ways and abandoned: (1) per-layer stroke overrides — only reach layers present on the DEFAULT swap target, so a richer glyph rendered half-tinted; (2) a variable-mode colour collection — Figma caps a collection at 10 modes and 13 icon colours are needed; (3) empty path-2 stubs so an override had somewhere to land — verified not to carry through a swap; (4) manual vectorPaths concatenation to force one path — CORRUPTED all 1,746 icons (see lesson) and forced a full rebuild; (5) figma.flatten + re-sync — geometry survived but the nested instances inside component-set variants became unreadable to the API. Stroke WEIGHT is unaffected and remains variable-driven and correct.
iconLibrary.apiCaveat: The plugin API cannot reliably read or write the subtree of an instance nested inside a COMPONENT-SET VARIANT — findAll() returns 0 vectors for 238 of 240 slots even though they render correctly on canvas. Only the set's DEFAULT variant is reachable. Page-level instances are fully reachable. Any per-variant nested styling must therefore be applied at instance-creation time, before the instance is inserted into the variant.

conventions: Marks are built the playbook's way: figma.createNodeFromSvg with the real lucide path data, rescaled by size/24 so the stroke keeps lucide's 2/24 ratio, and the inner vector named 'glyph' so the design-check lint does not flag it.
Every swatch is NAMED with its role and hex ('primary #6264f4'), so the layer list is readable as data and a hex can be copied without an inspector.
The mark gradient uses gradientTransform [[0.7071,0.7071,-0.2071],[-0.7071,0.7071,0.5]] — the 135deg diagonal the CSS uses. Horizontal ramps use [[1,0,0],[0,1,0]].

The hero bubble field is ELLIPSES with GRADIENT_RADIAL fills (opaque centre -> transparent edge) inside a clipped frame, not a multi-fill radial on one rect. A radial paint's default transform maps to the node's bounds, so an ellipse gives the bloom for free and each wash stays independently positionable.
'Infinite possibilities.' is a TEXT node with a GRADIENT_LINEAR fill — Figma fills text with a gradient natively, so the shipped --gradient-full-ramp is reproduced exactly rather than mocked.

Do not trust a counter you increment inside a fills.map() to prove a change landed — on the first sweep the aiden counter read 0 while the value had in fact changed. Read the resulting values back instead.

rebuild_2026_08_07.technique: DOM -> Figma. A browser-side extractor walks the rendered story and emits a compact scene graph (box / text / svg) with absolute geometry and computed paint; a Figma-side builder replays it as rectangles, TEXT nodes and createNodeFromSvg. Charts come over as real vectors, not images.
lessons: createNodeFromSvg resolves NO CSS - not currentColor, not var(--chart-1), not a stylesheet rule. Every paint must be burned into the markup as a literal attribute while the live element is still readable.
Chrome serialises color-mix() results as color(srgb r g b), which Figma's SVG parser rejects. Convert to rgb() before handing it over.

sr-only wrappers are 1x1 with overflow hidden, but their CHILDREN still report full-size rects - the chart's table twin was captured and painted over the chart. Prune any subtree whose own box is under 2px in BOTH axes.
A disc or pill carries its radius on a PARENT, so a filled child reads radius 0 and paints a square inside the circle. Inherit the ancestor radius when the child effectively fills it.
Figma's Inter measures wider than Chrome's, so text that is one line in the browser wraps here. Flag single-line text at extract time and let it self-size, re-anchoring by alignment.

CROSS-BRAND remapping is safe and cheap: within one mode the layout is identical, so a clone plus a ~13-pair colour map reproduces a sibling brand exactly (verified 1:1, zero conflicts). CROSS-MODE remapping is NOT safe - white maps to page, card AND ink, so each mode needs its own extract.
ec dark is the one brand whose chart slot 1 is not its --primary, so the blanket map paints its bars with the wrong blue. Its chart subtree and legend dot are corrected explicitly after the clone.

suite_built.bug_found_and_fixed_in_the_payloads: Every suite payload carried stop-color="circle" on lib entries 5 and 6. Cause: a CSS radial-gradient(circle at 50% 50%, ...) head has no explicit radii, so it does not match the `RW% RH% at X% Y%` shape the converter expects and falls through into the STOP LIST — the keyword became a colour. Perfectly parseable SVG, invalid paint, and invisible to every existing check. Stripped from all six files and a guard added to scripts/figma-build-dryrun.mjs (verified it bites: reintroducing one turns suite-light-1 from ok to failed=6 MISMATCH). Marketing was never affected — its radial gradients all use the explicit-radii form.
suite_built.known_defect_not_fixed: SIX text nodes in Suite render BLACK instead of their intended gradient: the four stat numbers (500K+, 2M+, 50B+, 99.9%) and both halves of the 'dart' wordmark. In dark mode they are effectively invisible. Cause is at EXTRACTION time, not replay: those elements use background-clip:text, so their computed `color` is transparent; rgba() returns null on zero alpha and the extractor falls back to [0,0,0,1]. Marketing has the same six black fallbacks but every one of them ALSO captured a `g` gradient, which overrides the fill — so it renders correctly and the bug stayed hidden. 'Infinite possibilities.' in Suite did capture its gradient and renders as the rainbow. Fix: re-extract Suite with the transparent-colour case handled, or hand-set those six fills in Figma.

brandRetirementSweep.lesson: A VARIABLE audit passing is not evidence that the FILE is correct. Deleting a variable mode silently orphans (a) every text label that named it, and (b) every node pinned to it, which falls back to the collection default and renders plausibly rather than erroring. languageSweep.gotcha: A DIRECT WRITE TO .characters SILENTLY FAILS when the text is driven by a component TEXT property. The first pass edited 152 text nodes and reported success; a verification sweep found 127 still unchanged, every one inside a _Doc/* instance (ids of the form I<inst>;<node>). Those values live on the INSTANCE as componentProperties, so the fix is setProperties() on the instance, not .characters on the inner node. Second pass patched 117 instances / 122 properties, and a third sweep confirmed zero remaining. Always verify a bulk text edit by re-scanning, never by the write count.
languageSweep.alsoNote: componentPropertyDefinitions cannot be read on a variant COMPONENT inside a set — only on the set or a standalone component. It throws, so guard it. 695 such throws in the first pass were harmless because the text edits ran before them in the same try block.

lessons: INSTANCE_SWAP via setProperties takes a NODE ID. A component key is REJECTED with "Property value is incompatible with component property type" — confirmed by a controlled test that tried both against the same icon. This matches the earlier addComponentProperty finding.

NOT EVERY NESTED GLYPH IS A PROPERTY. Mark's Glyph and Sidebar/MenuButton's icon do not surface on the parent instance's componentProperties, so setProperties silently does nothing and every tile renders the default. Both had to be swapped with swapComponent() on the nested INSTANCE. The rail shipped six identical chart glyphs until this was caught by LOOKING at it — no error was raised at any point.
Sidebar/MenuButton exposes no icon swap property at all; every instance defaults to Icon/house. Worth adding an INSTANCE_SWAP to that set — a nav is the one place every row needs a different icon.
TEXT CAN BE APPENDED INTO A SLOT inside an instance. The Recent rows' trailing app name is a real text node placed in ui-item__actions, which is what a slot is for.
appendChild() returns void — chaining `.name` onto it throws "cannot set property name of null".
layoutPositioning = ABSOLUTE requires the PARENT to have a layoutMode. A plain createFrame() badge slot throws; createAutoLayout() with a fixed size works.
